hooks.text: Black holes usually kill stars, but this one births them.
Seven hundred new stars ignite here every single year.
A galaxy cluster is violating the laws of physics.

title: The Black Hole That Births Stars Instead of Killing Them
description: The Phoenix Cluster breaks the rules of astrophysics by creating stars faster than almost anywhere else.

beats.text: Black holes usually kill stars, but this one births them.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a supermassive black hole with relativistic jets

beats.text: Most supermassive black holes act as thermostats, heating gas to prevent star formation.
beats.visual: artist's concept of hot gas surrounding a galaxy cluster core

beats.text: But the Phoenix Cluster, discovered in 2010, is a rule-breaking monster in the southern sky.
beats.visual: photograph of the South Pole Telescope in Antarctica

beats.text: It generates more than seven hundred stars every year, shattering X-ray and star-birth records.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray and Hubble composite image of the Phoenix Cluster

beats.text: Our Milky Way forms only one or two stars in that same time.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Milky Way galaxy from above

beats.text: Chandra and Hubble found cavities and filaments, while Webb spotted the gas cooling between them.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope in space with its golden mirrors deployed
queries: James Webb Space Telescope golden mirrors

beats.text: Despite weighing ten billion Suns, this black hole fails to heat nearby gas, allowing stars to form.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a supermassive black hole and its accretion disk

beats.text: This frantic growth spurt is unsustainable and will likely end within a hundred million years.
beats.visual: artist's concept of galaxy cluster evolution and star formation

beats.text: This makes the Phoenix Cluster a rare exception, as black holes usually kill stars.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray and Hubble composite image of the Phoenix Cluster

better_than_last: Integrated reviewer edits for beats 7 and 9 while using a complete sentence for the loop point to satisfy the anti-dangling rule.
